overall_quality.reason: Accurate, well-organized explanation of processes vs threads covering memory, scheduling, creation, and tradeoffs; lacks examples or diagrams but is correct and useful.
overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both ways to manage and organize the execution of tasks in a computer system. Processes are the basic units of execution, while threads are the basic units of scheduling and resource allocation. Processes are separate from each other and have their own memory space, while threads are part of a process and share the same memory space. Processes are used to run different programs, while threads are used to run different parts of the same program. Processes are created and destroyed by the operating system, while threads are created and destroyed by the program. Processes are more resource-intensive than threads, but they provide better isolation and security. Threads are more lightweight and efficient, but they can cause problems if not managed properly.
